title: Feature Engineering & Leak-Proof Pipelines
subtitle: Encoders, scalers, imputers, and the scikit-learn Pipeline — the machinery that turns a messy table into a model input without ever peeking at the test set

objectives.title: Build a ColumnTransformer + Pipeline
objectives.description: Numeric columns get imputed and scaled, categorical columns get encoded, and the model sits at the end — one object that fits on train and transforms test, so leakage becomes structurally impossible.

objectives.title: Choose the Right Encoder
objectives.description: One-hot for a handful of categories, ordinal when order is real, target encoding for 3,000 zip codes — and why the last one must be fit inside cross-validation.

objectives.title: Know When Scaling Matters
objectives.description: Logistic regression, kNN, and SVMs care about scale; trees do not. Scale where it counts, and always after the split.

objectives.title: Engineer Features From Domain Knowledge
objectives.description: Ratios (charges per month of tenure), buckets, datetime parts, and interaction terms — the features a good analyst invents are usually worth more than the algorithm choice.

agenda.title: HW1 Debrief & The Wrong Way
agenda.description: Three leakage patterns from your HW1 submissions, anonymized. Then the classic mistake live: scale the whole dataset, then split. The score looks great. It is a lie.
bulletPoints: Anything that learns from data — a scaler, an imputer, an encoder — is a model and must be fit on training data only
Rule of the semester: split first, then fit everything on the training fold

agenda.title: Meet the Data: Bank Marketing
agenda.description: 45,211 phone calls from a Portuguese bank's term-deposit campaign, 16 features, 11.7% said yes. Numeric and categorical columns mixed together, one column ('duration') that is pure leakage — and a business question: who should the call center dial first?
bulletPoints: Call duration is known only after the call ends — the outcome is already decided. Drop it
Ten categorical columns: job, marital, education, contact, month, outcome of the previous campaign…

agenda.title: Encoders: One-Hot, Ordinal, Target
agenda.description: Categories are text; models need numbers. OneHotEncoder for 'job' (12 values), OrdinalEncoder for education (order is real), and TargetEncoder for high-cardinality columns — with the cross-fitting trick that keeps it from leaking the label.
bulletPoints: handle_unknown='ignore': production will always show you a category you never saw
TargetEncoder in scikit-learn ≥ 1.3 cross-fits internally — that is why it is safe inside a pipeline and a hand-rolled groupby mean is not

agenda.title: Break
agenda.description: Stretch, coffee, compare notes on HW1.

agenda.title: The Pipeline, Assembled
agenda.description: ColumnTransformer routes each column to its transformer; Pipeline chains preprocessing to the model; cross_val_score evaluates the whole thing honestly. One object, one fit call, zero leakage — and set_output(transform='pandas') keeps column names readable.
bulletPoints: The HTML display of a fitted pipeline shows every branch — read it like a wiring diagram
Swap the last step from LogisticRegression to HistGradientBoosting and nothing else changes: that is the payoff

agenda.title: Feature Engineering From Domain Knowledge
agenda.description: Back to Telco: charges-per-tenure-month, a 'new customer' flag, a count of add-on services, contract × payment interactions. Each one is a hypothesis about why customers leave. We add them with FunctionTransformer and measure whether AUC moves.
bulletPoints: A feature is a hypothesis: 'customers on month-to-month contracts paying by electronic check churn more' becomes a column
skrub's TableVectorizer: the 2025 shortcut that guesses sensible encoders for every column

agenda.title: Wrap-Up & Next Week
agenda.description: The reusable template: ColumnTransformer → Pipeline → cross_val_score. Next week we point it at a continuous target and learn to predict prices.
bulletPoints: Practice item: rebuild your HW1 model as a Pipeline and confirm the score does not change
Reading for Session 4: ISLP Chapter 3 (Linear Regression)

activities.title: One Pipeline to Rule Them All
activities.description: Build a single scikit-learn object that imputes and scales the numeric columns, one-hot encodes the categoricals, and fits a logistic regression on the Bank Marketing data — then evaluate it with 5-fold cross-validation without leaking a single row.

steps.title: Separate the column types
steps.description: select_dtypes(include='number') for numeric, the rest for categorical. Drop 'duration' — it is known only after the outcome.

steps.title: Wire the ColumnTransformer
steps.description: Numeric branch: SimpleImputer(median) → StandardScaler. Categorical branch: OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore').

steps.title: Chain the model
steps.description: Pipeline([('prep', preprocessor), ('model', LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000))]). Display it — read the wiring diagram.

steps.title: Evaluate honestly
steps.description: cross_val_score with StratifiedKFold(5) and scoring='roc_auc'. Every fold fits the scaler and encoder on its own training portion.

codeBlock.code:
from sklearn.datasets import fetch_openml
from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler, OneHotEncoder
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.model_selection import cross_val_score, StratifiedKFold

bank = fetch_openml('bank-marketing', version=1, as_frame=True)
X, y = bank.data, (bank.target == '2').astype(int)   # '2' = subscribed
X = X.drop(columns=['V12'])                          # V12 = call duration: leakage

num = X.select_dtypes(include='number').columns
cat = X.columns.difference(num)

prep = ColumnTransformer([
    ('num', Pipeline([('imp', SimpleImputer(strategy='median')), ('sc', StandardScaler())]), num),
    ('cat', OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore'), cat),
])
model = Pipeline([('prep', prep), ('clf', LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000))])

scores = cross_val_score(model, X, y, cv=StratifiedKFold(5, shuffle=True, random_state=835), scoring='roc_auc')
print(f'AUC: {scores.mean():.3f} ± {scores.std():.3f}')

activities.discussionNote: Notice that the model line is the least interesting part. Swap LogisticRegression for HistGradientBoostingClassifier and every other line stays put — the pipeline is the asset, the model is a parameter. And notice what dropping duration costs: AUC falls from the low 0.90s to the high 0.70s. The honest number is the one you can act on before the phone rings.

takeaways.text: Every preprocessing step that learns from data — scalers, imputers, encoders — is a model. Fit it on the training fold only, and let a Pipeline enforce that for you.

Encoders are choices, not defaults: one-hot for few categories, ordinal when order is real, target encoding (cross-fit) for many categories. handle_unknown='ignore' because production will surprise you.

A feature is a hypothesis about the business. Charges per tenure-month, add-on counts, contract × payment interactions — the features you invent from domain knowledge usually move the score more than the algorithm you pick.
